docs.title: xgo_motorcortex2
docs.text: Kernel driver, display daemon, camera navigation (xgonav) and web UI for the XGO RiderPi: a self-balancing two-wheel robot with a Raspberry Pi CM4 (2 GB), an OV5647 wide-angle camera and an ESP32 motor controller.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Part Function Kernel driver xgo-drv talks to the ESP32 over UART, exposes /proc/XGORider/* (drive, height, IMU, wheels, LEDs, actions) xgonav camera pipeline: ego-motion, floor boundary (FloorNet), local map, room map, behaviours (follow, explore, home, patrol, pet) Web UI nginx + PHP on the Rider: live camera, manual driving, 3D attitude, room map, settings Display daemon eyes and emotions on the 320×240 LCD Firmware ESP32 firmware R-1.1.6 plus own patches, built with PlatformIO

Design rule: CPU time on the Rider comes first. Everything that only serves display or comfort runs in the browser or on the PC, never per frame on the CM4.

docs.title: Test status
docs.text:
Not a finished product

One device, one developer. Driven on the Rider: manual driving, follow, home (with start image check). explore ran three times and has no fall protection: it nearly drove down a step. approach and pet have only run in the simulator. Never run an autonomous mode near stairs. Details: Limitations.

docs.title: XGO Rider — LED meaning (firmware view)
docs.text: Applies to firmware R-1.1.6 (Rider2-recovered-full). Sources: board_support.cpp (renderLeds/renderFaultLeds), led_status.h (ledFaultFor), mode mapping in main.cpp. Stock firmware R-1.1.3 may differ (not analysed).

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
• 4 RGB LEDs (WS2812/NeoPixel) on GPIO27 (RMT channel 0), index 0..3.
  • Brightness: every output is multiplied by n/256. Stock ~0.5 (129), patch 0003 fixed 64, patch 0016: n settable at runtime (reg 0x12, !led <n>, Pi: settings/led_brightness), default 32, not stored across an ESP restart. Pi side stores the web value in /var/lib/xgonav/led_brightness (default 20 % = 51); rc.local sets it at boot, xgonav on start flashes 255 for 0.2 s, then sets it. "Full" colour values are usually 200–255.

docs.title: Priority
docs.text:
Per frame renderFaultLeds is tried first, otherwise renderLeds:

  1. Fault colour is shown unless robot_mode==1 (balancing) or robot_mode==250 (low battery), or there is no fault.
  2. Otherwise normal display (low-battery blink, gyro calibration, pitch trim, driving direction).
  3. Otherwise the user LEDs (patch 0023), balancing or not; redrawn when they or the brightness change.

LED effects are the client's business: the firmware shows states only. The colour gradients of the roll/height wave (actions 1, 2, 5, 6, registers 0x39/0x82) were removed with patch 0023.

Fault colour depends on last_stop_reason (ledFaultFor(driving,last_stop)), normal display on mode and drive/action values. All fields are in !status (mode, reason, last_stop_reason, driving).

docs.title: Power-on / ESP reset
docs.text: Colour Pattern Meaning Pink (R192 G0 B63), circling bright spot runs 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 (front left, rear left, rear right, front right), 0.4 s per turn, the others at 12 % Gyro boot calibration running (patch 0022, !ImuState::calibrated): keep the Rider still. ~1.5 s after power-on at standstill, up to ~15 s when moved, forever while \|roll\| ≥ 4°; again after an IMU fusion restart (then in the current user colours). Low battery, mode 0 and fault colours go first. Pink (R192 G0 B63), steady, all 4 constant Powered on / ESP reset / armed, gyro calibrated. begin() and arm() (action 255, stand-up 253, !arm) set the user LEDs to palette index 234; arming overwrites colours written by the client (patch 0023). Shown whenever no fault/stop colour, low battery, driving (green) or trim display is due.

docs.title: Fault / stop colours (Rider NOT standing, servos usually released)
docs.text: Colour Pattern Meaning (LedFault ← stop reason) Red, steady constant Tipped over / tilt fault. Also mode 0. Red, fast blink (~5 Hz) 100 ms on/off Free fall detected — stopped and servos released before impact. Red, slow blink (~1 Hz) 500 ms on/off Other fault: IMU, actuator, timing, invalid control output, policy or calibration fault. Servos released. Amber (R200 G70 B0), steady constant Manually stopped — !stop, action 0x3e=254, switch or app.

docs.title: Low battery
docs.text: Colour Pattern Meaning Red, blinking (battery timing) on/off with low_blink Battery empty / shutdown imminent (mode 250, stop_required). Own blink timing, not the fault patterns above. Stock: latched until power-off, all commands rejected. Patch 0026: clears after 5 s at ≥ 15 % (then mode 253), action 237 (ESP restart) accepted meanwhile.

docs.title: Normal operation (balancing, mode 1)
docs.text: Colour When Meaning User LEDs (default: pink, palette 234, all 4 the same) standing/balancing, not driving Idle. Colours via !rgb / registers 0x69–0x6c. Green, direction-dependent driving (|forward|>5 or |turn|>5) Forward → LEDs 0&3, backward → 1&2, left/right turn → two LEDs each.

docs.title: Pitch trim (mode 1)
docs.text: Colour When Meaning Blue blinking (~1 Hz) pitch_trim_stage==2 Pitch trim running (balancing in place).

docs.title: Mode → situation (!status.mode)
docs.text: mode Situation LED 1 balancing / driving user LEDs, green direction 0 tilt/fall fault, "stranded", runaway protection red (tilt = steady, fall = fast blink) 250 battery empty / shutdown red blinking (battery timing) 251 actuator fault / flash stop red slow blink (Other) 252 policy/control fault red slow blink (Other) 253 after flash / ready but disarmed / neutral fault colour of the current guard reason (e.g. red while tipped), otherwise user LEDs (pink after power-on and after arming) 254 manual stop amber 255 leg calibration running (calibration mode)

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text:
• Red = problem/stopped (pattern gives cause: steady = tip, fast = fall, slow = fault, battery timing = battery).
  • Amber = deliberately stopped.
  • Green = driving (direction).
  • Blue = pitch trim.
  • Pink circling = gyro calibrating, keep still.
  • Pink = powered on / armed, or idle with default user LEDs.
  • Other steady colour = idle (user LEDs set via !rgb / leds/0..3).

Read state live: !status → mode, driving, reason, last_stop_reason. Set LEDs (visible whenever no state display is due, also while lying; reset to pink by arming): !rgb <index 0..3> <r> <g> <b> or registers 0x69–0x6c (/proc/XGORider/leds/0..3).

docs.title: Per-frame data flow (App._step(), xgonav/app.py)
docs.text:
camera.FrameSource ─► egomotion.EgoMotion ─► tracker.Tracker ◄── detector.DetectorWorker (thread)
                            │                       │
                            ├─► imu.imu_frame (IMU at frame time, one value per frame → pitch_dev, roll, heading)
                            ├─► freespace.FreeSpaceWorker: FloorNet (thread) ─► localmap.LocalMap
                            ├─► wheels (odometry) ─► gridmap.GridMap (thread, display only)
                            ▼
              behaviors.World ─► Behavior.step() ─► behaviors.safety() ─► App._arc_check() ─► robot.Robot.drive()

docs.title: Clock rates
docs.text: Loop Rate Does Image loop camera fps (camera.fps = 24) ego-motion, tracker update, free space, snapshot Control step control_hz = 24 Hz (sim: 20), at the frame nearest to the beat (threshold 1/control_hz − 0.5/fps), so at most the frame rate: RiderPi every frame. Until 2026-11-17 control_hz 20 gave only every 2nd frame (~12 Hz) on the Rider: the 50 ms threshold was reached only at the second frame (41.7 ms apart). 24 Hz not installed, not driven build World, run behaviour, safety, drive() Detector detector.max_hz (RiderPi: 5 Hz), only in follow/approach/pet YOLO on sharp frames, own thread; recognition only, never obstacles IMU / wheels firmware stream imu.stream_hz (100 Hz); without stream 50 Hz polling of 0x0d (imu.imu_hz) kernel thread, read from /proc/XGORider/imu_log, wheels_log

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Only the newest frame counts. FrameSource.get() drops old frames. No queues.
  • Ego-motion is removed everywhere: per frame a homography A = K·Rᵀ·K⁻¹ (rotation model: yaw/pitch/roll + expansion), applied to all tracks; delayed detections are shifted with EgoMotion.transform_between(a, b); horizon line and ground-point distance use pitch_dev.
  • Display reads snapshots only: App.snapshot is replaced per frame (never mutated), signalled via snap_cond. Web, LCD and recorders (--record, --record-raw) read from it; render() draws the overlay on demand.

docs.text:
Role Real Simulator/test Image source camera.PiCameraSource, camera.OpenCVSource sim.SimWorld Robot robot.ProcRobot robot.SimRobot Detector detector.DetectorWorker sim.FakeDetector (ground truth, 180 ms latency, 5 Hz) IMU imu.ProcImu sim.SimImu Floor boundary floornet.FloorNet sim.SimFloorNet (ground truth of the rendered frame; sim.Phantoms adds false alarms)

docs.title: Safety layers (in order, last word wins)
docs.text:
Layer Action behaviors.safety() not balancing → stop; blind (no FloorNet) → stop; centre free space < blocked_free·0.6 → no forward; < slow_free → scale v (≥ 0.25); TTC < ttc_stop_s (0.8 s) → no forward App._arc_check() planned arc (forward and reverse) checked against local map Robot clamp to max_v/max_w, ramp (accel_v, accel_w), keepalive 0.3 s, userspace watchdog stall_timeout_s 0.5 s Kernel settings/motion_timeout_ms (xgonav sets robot.kernel_watchdog_ms = 1000)

manual mode skips floor model and arc check; fall detection and watchdogs stay active.

docs.title: Robot convention
docs.text:
• drive(v, w): normalised [-1, 1]; v > 0 forward, w > 0 turn left.
  • robot.norm_to_u8: u8 = 255/(2L)·(v + L), 128 = standstill.
  • Firmware holds setpoints; stops must be written explicitly.
  • robot.reverse_gain multiplies negative v before sending, robot.manual_forward_gain positive v in manual mode only (RiderPi: 2.0 each).
  • robot.speed_ctrl: App._speed_tick (control step) compares wheel speed with the target, robot.SpeedCtrl integrates the difference, Robot._send adds it after the gains. Firmware speed loop is P only, so the Rider runs slower on carpet without it.

docs.text: Thread Cores Main loop, camera, OpenCV workers 0–1 YOLO (NCNN: thread + OpenMP pool on 2–3; onnxruntime: caller on 2, pool on 3) 2–3 Free-space worker, grid worker 2–3 Web/LCD rendering, raw recording 0–3

docs.title: Microphones
docs.text:
Measured 2026-11-13 on the RiderPi, quiet room.

Item Value Count 2 microphones, stereo (left = LINPUT1, right = RINPUT1) Record arecord -D hw:0,0 -f S16_LE -r 48000 -c 2 out.wav (works while pipewire/wireplumber run as aeinstein) Silence both channels ≈ −27 dBFS noise at full gain, no zero samples; channels uncorrelated (0.09) Noise spectrum 50–66 % below 200 Hz (hum / structure-borne), ~28 % above 12 kHz, whine at 15.9 kHz in both channels Own speaker (freude.wav, 1.0–1.8 kHz) +43 dB (×145) over silence on both channels, L/R correlation 0.99, same level Placement close together: equal level and near-identical signal from the own speaker; direction at best coarse

docs.title: Sound direction (xgonav/ortung.py)
docs.text:
Time difference left/right from the phase of the cross spectrum (GCC-PHAT, 300–2000 Hz), angle from asin(c·(τ − tau_offset) / mic_dist_m). The microphones are acoustically only ≈ 4 mm apart (τ ≤ ±11 µs, one sample = 21 µs): usable only averaged over ≈ 1 s, i.e. for speech and steady sounds, not for a single clap.

Item Value Output GET /status → ortung.letzter: winkel_deg (0 = centre, > 0 left), tau_us, guete 0..1, pegel_db, alter_s; ortung.verlauf (last sounds, for the radar card in the web page, web-interface.md); in code app.ortung.last (Schall) Limits two microphones: left/right only, front and back are the same (a source at 150° reads as 30°) Active [ortung] modes (idle, pet), never in sleep mode or during Wi-Fi setup; arecord on hw:0,0 runs only then (device opens once: arecord by hand fails meanwhile; mode manual frees it) Gate per 1024-sample block (21 ms) one level value (band ≈ 0.7–3.5 kHz) against a tracked noise floor: opens at on_db = 9, stays open down to off_db = 3, pauses ≤ hang_blocks (0.25 s) do not end a sound. A steady sound is followed for ≈ 15 s, then counts as silence (noise_up) Estimate open gate: one FFT per block (both channels as one complex signal), cross spectrum summed over ≤ 47 blocks (1 s), weighted |S|^-0.8, tested against 41 delays within ±17 µs, parabola at the peak; sounds < 0.5 s dropped Own sounds ignored while aplay from xgonav runs and nachhall_s = 0.3 after; sounds started elsewhere (web, rc.local) are not Cost separate arecord process (0.1 % of a core) plus one thread; C++ core native/ortfast.cpp (status kern). CM4 at 600 MHz (powersave, 2026-11-13): 39 µs per quiet block (≈ 0.2 % of a core in silence), 146 µs per FFT block (≈ 0.7 % while a sound lasts), 211 µs per estimate; numpy fallback 317 / 284 / 722 µs. C++ equal to numpy there (max. difference 3e-19 s). Nothing in the frame loop Tools python tools/ortung.py live on the Rider (xgonav in sleep mode or a mode outside [ortung] modes), tools/ortung.py wav file.wav for a stereo recording; test tone for a phone: band noise 300–2000 Hz, 1.5 s on / 0.5 s off

docs.title: Calibration 2026-11-13 (balancing, test tone 1 m ahead, turned on the spot in 8 steps)
docs.text:
τ = 11.2 µs · sin(angle) − 2.2 µs, residual 0.6 µs (300–2000 Hz, 1 s windows) → mic_dist_m = 0.0038, tau_offset_us = -2.2. Scatter per estimate: 0.13 s ±6 µs, 0.5 s ±3 µs, 1 s ±1–2 µs, 2 s ±0.7–1.3 µs.

Source at −1° −44° −97° −150° +162° +119° +71° +22° expected (front/back folded) −1° −44° −83° −30° +18° +61° +71° +22° reported, median of 9–10 +2° −56° −90° −32° +21° +57° +60° +23°

Same code on the recordings set down with the TV 2–3 m away (smooth, sloping walls): 90° left +15°, 45° left +16°, ahead +14°, 90° right −24°. Lying down only "right" stands out; use the direction while balancing.

Above 2 kHz the channels are not phase-true: at 3.5–4.5 kHz the phase sits at ≈ ±165° whatever the direction (coherence 0.4–0.7). With the first band (500–5000 Hz, 0.13 s windows) this produced apparent delays of −80…−100 µs for every source; those angles meant nothing.

docs.title: Voice samples (xgonav/stimme.py, mode pet)
docs.text:
The pet learns phrases it hears repeatedly and parrots them back, filtered to sound like a budgie. Not yet tried on the Rider (2026-11-19).

Item Value Capture on the [ortung] stream (Ortung.horcher), only in pet (balancing or lying) while a person is in view or gone ≤ [pet] parrot_listen_s (3 s); never during own sounds (+ nachhall_s) VAD ortung level vs. noise floor: opens vad_on_db 6, ends after vad_hang_s 0.6 s below vad_off_db 4 (hang-over; 0.3 s split phrases); vad_pre_s 0.3 s pre-roll; 0.3–3 s (cut at max_s; 0.6 s lost short phrases like "Komm her") Features 48 kHz stereo → 16 kHz mono (FIR 7 kHz), 13 MFCC per 10 ms, edges more than trim_db 12 dB below the loudest frame trimmed (with 20 dB the noise of pre-roll/hang-over stayed in), mean removed; rejected if < voiced_min 0.4 of the frames within laut_db 10 dB of the loudest are voiced: flatness 300–3000 Hz < flat_max 0.3 and pitch 70–400 Hz (autocorrelation from the power spectrum, window-corrected) > per_min 0.5. Rider 2026-11-19 (kettle running): speech 0.45–1.0, kettle alone 0.12–0.29, running water 0.0–0.26 (with flatness only and 0.3, water noise got learned) Match DTW (Sakoe-Chiba 25 %, length ratio ≤ 1.6), cost per step ≤ match_dist 8. Labelled recording on the Rider (3 phrases × 5, kettle running, tools/stimme.py strom): same phrase 5.1–8.2, different phrases ≥ 8.8, mostly 9.5–12. Windows TTS: same phrase other rate 2–4, other phrases ≥ 14 Learning no match → candidate (≤ pool_n 30); a candidate not confirmed within kandidat_max_min 1 min is deleted (thread checks every 5 s); match with a candidate → confirmed (louder take kept), filtered, parroted after parrot_delay_s 0.2 s (after the 0.6 s hang-over: ≈ 0.9 s after the end of speech); match with a confirmed one → parroted again, every time. At max_confirmed 10 a new confirmation replaces the confirmed sample heard least often (tie: longest not heard); counts in bestaetigt/zaehler.json Budgie filter noise gate first (gate_db 12 below the loudest frame, knee_db 6, silent edges cut; without it 57–86 % of a sample was kettle noise and sounded like gurgling water), pitch_st +12 semitones at the same tempo (WSOLA: stretch ×2 with 30 ms pieces matched by cross-correlation ±10 ms, then play ×2 faster; formants move up too), ×speed 1.0 (user: not faster), vibrato 25 Hz ±0.3 ms, high-pass 1 kHz + low-pass 5 kHz, tanh drive 2, peak −3 dB, 10 ms fades; once per confirmation Playback when talking back (brabbeln) a learned sample instead with parrot_p 0.5, ≥ parrot_repeat_s 30 s apart, least played first (sound stimme:NN) Files [stimme] dir (/opt/xgonav/stimmen): kandidaten/<time>.wav (16 kHz raw), bestaetigt/NN_roh.wav, NN.wav (48 kHz filtered); delete the directory to forget everything Status GET /status → ortung.stimme (aufnahme, bestaetigt, kandidaten, voll, segmente, verworfen, wieder); pet info nachgeplappert, proben Cost per 21 ms block only while capturing: a few comparisons and keeping the block; per utterance C++ core native/stimmfast.cpp in thread stimme (CM4: 3 s features ≈ 21 ms before the pitch check, DTW ≈ 2 ms per sample); filter once per confirmation (≈ 6 ms per s). numpy fallback equal to rounding (1e-13). docs.title: Bluetooth (BLE)
docs.text:
Own GATT service of the ESP32 firmware (patch 0025). Replaces the vendor service fff0/fff1/fff2; the vendor app no longer finds the Rider.

Device name RiderKerk (fixed in the firmware; flash sector 0x320000 is no longer read or written) Advertising name + service UUID Security none: no pairing, no bonding, no encryption. Anyone in radio range can drive the Rider and set the Wi-Fi; the Wi-Fi password crosses the air in clear text MTU ESP32 offers 185; request ≥ 185 (Android: requestMtu(247)). Works with 23, large replies are then slow Status flashed and installed on the RiderPi 2026-11-20 ~19:00 (lying). Seen there: advertising as RiderKerk with the service UUID, register 0x18 = address of wlan0, one tunnel request from a BLE client answered (driver counters). Confirmed by the user with the Android app the same evening: connect, IP shown, web page opened. CMD, CON, wlan connect and throughput not yet checked

docs.title: Service
docs.text:
Service fdacc797-7e1d-4d87-9205-64ca79f74500. Characteristics: same base, last byte as below. Every notify characteristic has a CCCD (0x2902).

Characteristic UUID … Properties Content CMD …4501 write, write without response, notify binary frames of the serial protocol, replies by notify CON …4502 write, write without response, notify text console of the firmware: line in, text out PI …4503 write, write without response, notify byte tunnel to the Pi (Wi-Fi, xgonav) IP …4504 read, notify IPv4 of the Pi, 4 bytes a.b.c.d

Notifications are a byte stream cut at arbitrary points (MTU − 3 per packet): reassemble by frame length (CMD), line (CON) or reply header (PI). On disconnect the firmware sets forward and turn to neutral and drops unsent output.

docs.title: IP
docs.text: Source driver xgo-drv writes the address of wlan0 (settings/ip_dev) to register 0x18 on change and every 3 s 0.0.0.0 no address, or nothing from the Pi for 10 s (Pi off, driver not loaded) Needs driver only; works without xgo-ble and without xgonav Also read register 0x18 over CMD; pi_ip in !status

docs.title: CMD: binary frames
docs.text:
Same protocol as the Pi UART (docs/driver.md, firmware/README.md).

55 00 LEN TYPE REG DATA… CHK 00 AA      LEN = bytes of DATA + 8 (≤ 32), CHK = ~(LEN + TYPE + REG + ΣDATA)
TYPE Meaning 01 write REG (no reply; result text in !status → result) 02 read REG, DATA = 1 byte (ignored); reply TYPE 12 with the register's fixed length Example Frame read battery (0x01) 55 00 09 02 01 01 F2 00 AA → 55 00 09 12 01 57 8C 00 AA (87 %) stop / sit down (action 254) 55 00 09 01 3E FE B9 00 AA LED 0 red (0x69) 55 00 0B 01 69 FF 00 00 8B 00 AA

Not over BLE: register 0x11 (IMU stream, Pi only), telemetry stream 0x08, registers 0x17/0x18 writes (Pi only). Removed with 0025: 0x13 (name suffix), 0xb3 (trace stream).

Action 254 written directly does not stop xgonav: send nav POST /stop first, otherwise mode pet makes it jump up again after a faint.

docs.title: CON: console
docs.text:
One command per line, terminated by \n, at most 95 characters. Same commands as on USB (!status, !stop, !arm, !standup, !restart, !move F T, !height N, !led N, !balance N, !rgb I R G B, !fallguard …, !liftguard …, !gain X, …; unknown line → command list). Output of !trace dump / !trace usb on still goes to USB.

!status one JSON line, ~3.5 kB Output buffer 4 kB; more is dropped Commands without output most setters; check result in !status

docs.title: PI: tunnel to the Pi
docs.text:
Path: PI ↔ ESP32 ↔ UART ↔ xgo-drv (/proc/XGORider/ble) ↔ service xgo-ble. Needs driver and xgo-ble, not xgonav (except nav), not a network.

Request: one UTF-8 line, terminated, ≤ 1023 bytes. <id> = token chosen by the client (≤ 16 characters), echoed in the reply. One request at a time; replies come in request order.

<id> wlan status
<id> wlan scan
<id> wlan rescan
<id> wlan connect <WPA|NOPASS> <0|1> <ssid> [<password>]
<id> nav <GET|POST> <path?query>

Reply: header line, then exactly n bytes of body.

<id> <code> <n>
<body>
Request code Body wlan status exit code of xgo-wlan (0 = ok) con=, ssid=, ip=, in hotspot mode (RiderKerk) clients= and letzt= (last failed connect); one key=value per line wlan scan 〃 visible networks from the NetworkManager cache, SIGNAL:SECURITY:SSID per line (: inside an SSID is escaped as \:) wlan rescan 〃 same after a fresh scan (several seconds) wlan connect 0 = connected, 1 = failed on success as status; on failure the reason as last line. Replies after the attempt (up to ~60 s; client timeout ≥ 90 s). On failure the Pi returns to the previous connection nav HTTP status of xgonav; 599 = xgonav not running reply body, cut at 16 384 bytes any 400 = not understood, 403 = path not allowed text wlan connect field WPA / NOPASS WPA/WPA2/WPA3 personal with password (8–63 characters) / open network 0 / 1 1 = hidden SSID ssid, password percent-encoded (space = %20, % = %25, non-ASCII as UTF-8 bytes); no line breaks

nav passes the request to the xgonav HTTP interface on 127.0.0.1:8088 (docs/web-interface.md): /status, /stop, /mode?name=…, /drive?v=…&w=…, /pipeline?on=…, … Not allowed: /ws, /frame, /map.png. Movement rules are those of xgonav (/drive only in mode manual, modes need the floor net).

Example (phone → Rider, Rider → phone):

1 wlan status
                         1 0 41
con=xgo-Heim
ssid=Heim
ip=192.168.53.110

2 wlan connect WPA 0 Mein%20Netz geheim123

                                        2 0 48
con=xgo-Mein Netz
ssid=Mein Netz
ip=10.10.0.110

3 nav POST /mode?name=idle
            3 200 <n>
<reply of xgonav>

After a successful wlan connect the new address also arrives as IP notification (within ~3 s). Web interface: https://<ip>/ (self-signed certificate, no login; port 80 redirects).

Throughput (by design, not measured): Pi → phone ~4.6 kB/s, phone → Pi a little more (UART shared with the 100 Hz IMU stream). Disconnect: xgo-ble drops a half-received line; a running wlan connect finishes anyway.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
Run on the Rider in /opt/xgonav with venv/bin/python. Results go into /opt/xgonav/config.toml by hand. Order matters: FOV first.

Positioning helpers (balancing Rider): 

python tools/nudge.py turn <deg>     # IMU-controlled, + = left
python tools/nudge.py move <s>       # open loop, + = forward

docs.title: 0. Horizontal FOV — [camera] hfov_deg
docs.text: Item Value Default 91.8° (RiderPi, f = 310 px at 640 px); RPi camera v1 would be 62.2° RiderPi measured (2026-11-07) turns on the spot against IMU heading (IMU = 99.6–99.8 % of true angle over full turns): rotation fit with fixed IMU yaw 304–310 px, ORB pairs 25–45° apart 310–313 px in three recordings → 91.8°. Lens distortion negligible (k1 −0.010…+0.003, ≤ 2 px at the edge, ~4 px in the corner) Earlier values 88.5° (f 328.3 px) from the folding rule (section 2a) with measured h = 100 mm: that method only fixes f·h, the 5.6 % gap means h was ~106 mm. Checkerboard on a display gave 297–316 px Driving direction (2026-11-08) focus of expansion while driving straight: 16 segments ≥ 1.5 m from 8 drives (45 m), rotation per frame pair estimated, FOE shared per segment → column 333.8 (MAD 16, SE ~4; ≥ 2.5 m: 332.2). Camera looks ~2.4° left of the driving direction → [camera] lens_yaw_deg = 2.40 (formerly cx_offset_px = 13), rotated out in the undistortion table. Mounting roll 1.25° → lens_roll_deg (formerly [imu] roll_ref_deg). A second Rider only needs its own lens block (distortion, roll, yaw); pitch stays tilt_deg. Simulator check ±3 px. Roll not measured (stripe board: ~1.5°) Check yaw/roll (2026-11-18) folding rule on the floor under the camera along the driving direction must lie on the web overlay "Image centre" (column W/2); a floor joint at right angles to it must be level. Confirmed with lens_yaw_deg = 2.40, lens_roll_deg = 1.25 (Rider lying). Use one rule segment only (the hinges kink ~1°); re-align after the Rider stood up Wrong FOV effect all angles from the image (ego yaw/pitch, tracker shift, object bearing) scale with f: with 88.5° they were ~5 % too small Floor distances depend on f·h: after changing f, re-measure camera height (mount_offset_mm), else distances shrink ~6 % Method turn ≥ 360° on the spot and compare image rotation with IMU heading, or checkerboard + cv2.calibrateCamera

docs.title: 2. Camera height and tilt — [camera] mount_offset_mm, tilt_deg, [imu] pitch_ref_deg
docs.text:
Item Value Height, direct measurement lens centre above floor while balancing, at two or more height set-points → cam_h_u8 = [a, b] (mm = a + b·u8) RiderPi (2026-11-07) u8 106 / 150 / 200: wheel axle 31 mm (2026-11-08 exact: wheel diameter 60 mm, hub 30 mm above the floor), leg pivot 87 / 91 / 98 mm, lens centre 122 / 125 / 132–133 mm → cam_h_u8 = [109.4, 0.1126] (residuals ≤ 1.3 mm). Camera sits rigidly 35 mm above the leg pivot Why not body height + offset the body height in mm (60–120 over u8 0–255) rises 22 mm from u8 106 to 200, the real body only 11 mm; the old mount_offset_mm = 43 (128 mm at u8 106) put the camera 18 mm too high at u8 200 Floor check (2026-11-07) tape front edges 0.48 / 0.98 m from wheel contact, raw frames at u8 106 and 200, camera 36 mm ahead of contact (CAD): horizon off −0.05° / +0.08°, f·h too large by factor 1/0.926 / 1/0.921 (distances ~7.5 % too far) Grid check (2026-11-10) printed grid (tools/pruefmuster.py, 50 mm, 950 mm across the sheet joints) flat on the floor, balancing, 39 raw frames each: lens height = distance of a floor point from the grid's vanishing line ÷ lateral px/mm at that point (no camera model, no distance needed) → 124–126 mm at u8 128, 131–133 mm at u8 205 (spread < 1 mm); horizon row from the grid 254 / 251 vs. 255.5 / 248.5 in xgonav. Grid on the wall at 0.40 / 0.75 m: f 307–313 px from the 350 mm shift, pixels square within 0.5 %, distortion −3.6 px at r 220 px, about −10 px in the corners (not a single k1). Row check with the whole grid in view (u8 205, wheel contact 310 mm before the first line, 9 cross lines 0.31–0.71 m, pitch free per frame): ground_dist with f 310 and h 132.5 mm fits the centre column within 0.7 px and puts the horizon at row 247.1 (xgonav at that moment 247.0–247.8); with h × 0.921 the residuals are −3.7…+2.2 px and the horizon lands at 253.9. Towards the right image edge the fitted f·h rises to +4 % (Rider not square to the grid or distortion, not separated). Sets where the wheel position was only estimated to ±2 mm near the first line gave ±4–8 % and are not used RiderPi value cam_h_u8 = [109.4, 0.1126] = the direct measurement, confirmed by the grid check. The factor 0.921 from the tape check (used 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-10) is dropped; why the tape check differed is open CAD check docs/Rider-Pi.STEP with the leg linkage of tools/step_to_model.py: lens 122.6 mm at u8 106 when the floor is taken at the tyre (radius 31.5 mm), rise 12.4 mm to u8 200 Tilt from wall base line RiderPi tilt_deg = 1.39 at raw IMU pitch -2.7° (R-1.1.3, board + 2 wall measurements, spread 0.25°) R-1.1.6 pitch_ref_deg = -0.5, set visually on the horizon line; wall measurement open 

python tools/calibrate.py wall --cols 0.45:0.55 --debug wand.jpg   # Rider facing a wall, ~1 m
python tools/calibrate.py wall ...                                 # second position, ~2 m
python tools/calibrate.py solve <row1>:<m1> <row2>:<m2>
- Distance = wheel contact point → wall base, measured after standing up (Rider rolls ~20 cm forward). - Check the debug image: shadow at the wall base → floor model measures the shadow edge. - tilt_deg and pitch_ref_deg are a pair; enter both. - Long exposure allowed for this (exposure_us = 33000).

docs.title: 2a. Folding-rule method (2026-11-04, no wall, no display)
docs.text: Item Value Setup rule A along the camera axis, rule B across (2 m, centred) at 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 m; distance wheel contact point → front edge of B Per position 40 raw frames (/frame?raw=1) averaged + IMU pitch; Rider resting still (disarmed, leaning back) is ideal — no sway Model row(D) = cy + f·tan(atan(h / (D + 8 mm + e)) − τ), cy = 240; fit e, τ and f (with measured h) Degeneracy rows alone only fix f·h → measure camera height h directly RiderPi h = 100 mm (measured), rows 338.2 / 303.3 / 292.3 / 286.3 → f = 328.3 px (hfov 88.5°), horizon row 269.8 = 5.18° up at IMU pitch −4.43°, residuals ≤ 0.24 px Result hfov_deg = 88.5, tilt_deg = 5.18, pitch_ref_deg = -4.43; mount_offset_mm needs camera height while balancing at known body height (still 43). Superseded for f by section 0 (91.8°); f·h from this fit stays valid

docs.title: 2c. Time offset frame → IMU — [imu] time_offset_ms, pitch_sign
docs.text:
Both are fixed in the defaults since 2026-11-17 (-1, 10.5); the online estimate (ImuSync) runs only with 0 / None (simulator).

Every consumer (geometry, floor model roll, map heading, tilt, overlay, web) uses one IMU value per frame: imu.imu_frame at frame time (SensorTimestamp) + time_offset_ms, linearly interpolated in the imu_log history. Measure the offset on the PC from a raw recording (web button Aufzeichnen, needs pitch motion such as height changes):

python tools/imu_versatz.py ~/fahrt/<recording> [--fenster idx,idx,... --halb 48]
Date Result 2026-11-17 recording 20261117-161237 (height changes), 8 sections of 4 s: +9.9..+12.0 ms, all together +10.5 ms, sign −1, correlation 0.99; slope 1.13 (image pitch 13 % larger than IMU pitch: focal length or IMU scale, open)

Web: the line under the camera image shows the IMU value of each frame (pitch, roll, heading, sample age, pitch rate image vs. IMU) and counts frames without a valid IMU value (red). Drift check: Bild am IMU-Nick festhalten (camera bar) shifts each frame in the browser by row_stand − row_imu (normal pose against the pure IMU pitch; black border, no load on the pipeline); the cyan line is then fixed. Scene moving against it = IMU or time-sync drift.

docs.text:
With firmware patches up to 0010 both directions respond alike (register 0x0e, 2026-11-05: wheel speed per target 2.67 forward, 2.65 reverse). Sent 0.12: 26 cm/s, sent 0.24: 50 cm/s. RiderPi uses 2.0 for both; forward only in manual mode. Table below: 2026-11-02.

Command (2 s) Distance u8 147 (v = +0.15) 86 cm forward u8 109 (v = −0.15) 4 cm backward u8 90 (v = −0.15, reverse_gain = 2.0) ≈ forward distance (by eye)

Backward command: Rider leans 2–3°, overshoots forward when stopping.

docs.title: Mode pet (xgonav/pet.py)
docs.text:
Started by hand (web UI „Haustier“, --mode pet). Not run on the Rider yet, see limitations.md.

Trigger Reaction person > 3 m notices, chirp person 1.5–3 m turns toward, tilts head (roll), doubt; a drive command (v ≠ 0, not turning) sets roll back to 0 and levels once (Robot.request_level, 2026-11-22) person < 1.5 m cute, trill, wiggle person < ~0.5 m shy, ducks box top free and < 1.9 m (kneeling, sitting, child) like person approaching > ~1 m/s within 1.6 m surprised, squeak, duck, optional jerk back person gone < 3 s and back laugh, giggle person gone > 3 s looks after them, doubt, searches (below), sad if not found wheels move without a drive command embarrassed, „hey“ nobody for 30 s (roam_after_s, again every 45 s) roams (below) nobody for 60 s / 180 s / 600 s sighs / dozes, detector 1 Hz, roaming ends / sets down, idle cat turns toward, like, coo; optional creep up to 0.8 m dog within 2 m (priority over all) keeps looking, grievance, whimper, duck, optional jerk back dog < 0.5 m or hard scare (with faint) faint, see below

Eyes follow the bearing of the target, gliding one position per control step; once the same person has been fixated for eyes_fix_s (1.5 s, gaze arrived) the lids narrow to slits (eyes_fix_lid 2, 2026-11-22). They blink through all lid positions in 0.4 s (atlas, neutral eye style without pupils, replaces the overlay on the LCD; written only when changed, checked at ~33 Hz). Priority: dog, cat, person. Trust (0..1) shifts thresholds; repeated scares weaken (habituation).

docs.title: Search and roam
docs.text:
Tasks inside state wach; any person/cat/dog in view ends them (search: like + found sound; roam: surprised). Position from wheels and heading (World.yaw), independent of the room map; reset on stand-up.

Task Sequence follow (any person in view whose box is not wider than tall; no trust threshold; 2026-11-22) exactly the routine of mode follow (behaviors.Follow inside Pet): behavior.follow_dist_m 0.9 m, speed, backwards up to backup_v when she comes too close, heights, detector at its full rate; lost → drives to the last place and looks around (map), without map turns to the last side. Ends when follow waits (lost_home: then home), animal in view, she sits/lies, no drive allowed (follow_m, battery, floor); new start after follow_repeat_s. Person lying/sitting (box wider than tall): no following, turns toward her, trust grows, babbles every wide_babble_s 6 s with head tilt. Simulator (--scene zwei) and unit tests only search (person gone > gone_s, or lost while following) drive to seek_stop_m (0.4 m) short of the last foot-point position (planner with room map), at most seek_m → look around → sad, lost sound. Sound is ignored while driving there and looking around; afterwards he stays and listens (normal hearing), no drive home (lost_home false, 2026-11-22) roam (nobody for roam_after_s) look around, note free space per view → leg of roam_leg_m (0.4 m) toward the freest view within roam_radius_m (1.0 m) of the stand-up spot (none: back toward it) → look around → … until roam_m is used up; new budget after each encounter look around look_steps (4) views, look_step_deg (90°) apart, look_pause_s (1.5 s) standing still each (detector, floor model); eyes sweep. Turning only, on by default (look, needs gestures)

Driving (seek_m, roam_m, roam_radius_m: 0 = off, −1 = no limit; RiderPi default −1 since 2026-11-13, simulator 0 / 0 / 1.0 m) only forward at drive_v (0.08), with wheels, valid floor model + local map, battery ≥ roam_battery (40 %). Stops on: remaining distance within coast (~0.9 s × speed), budget, arc check of the local map blocked (path_blocked, computed only while driving), centre free space < half roam_free_min, no progress for 2.5 s, time-out. Three failed legs end roaming. Foot points > 5 m (occluded) are ignored, distances capped at 3.5 m. Steps are seen too late by the floor model: never near stairs. Pi cost: arithmetic per control step, plus one arc check per control step while driving.

docs.title: Hearing (sound direction, audio.md)
docs.text:
Input: reports of xgonav/ortung.py (≈ 1 per second of sound, direction folded to the front). Direction counts only while balancing and only if the 1 s window began after his own last movement. [pet] hear = false turns all of it off. Unit tests only, not run on the Rider (2026-11-13).

Situation Reaction sound from the side, nobody in view eyes move there, sound horch, turns to it at once (look_w; a sound near the front needs two reports, with hear_seek one), listens hear_listen_s (3.5 s). After a listen he turns again only after hear_repeat_s (6 s), unless the sound comes from ≥ hear_side_deg (45°) to the left or right (2026-11-14). Again from the side → the source was behind: turns by the remainder (180° − reading); at most hear_turns (3). From the front → done. Silence → doubt, then searches (hear_seek, below) sound while roaming (he turns and drives almost all the time, no direction then) stops roaming, stands and listens; the next report gives the direction target appears while turning surprised, found sound; then talks back (below) come here: a person in view farther than come_stop_m + 0.3 m speaks (come_events = 1 report, a short call is enough) happy sound, drives toward the person and stops come_stop_m (0.4 m since 2026-11-22, was 0.8) short, following while they move; no planner path → straight toward her, at most 30 s; at most come_m per time (RiderPi −1 = no limit, simulator 0), again after come_repeat_s (8 s). Ends when the person is lost for 1 s (then the normal search) or the arc is blocked calling: voice keeps coming from the front (call_events = 3 reports), nobody in view searches there like "search": drives at most call_m (RiderPi −1 = no limit, then one 3 m leg per call; never more than seek_m; simulator 0) with the same conditions as every pet drive, then looks around (finds someone standing exactly behind). Again after call_repeat_s (45 s) at the earliest heard, then silence, nobody in view (hear_seek, 2026-11-19) direction known (turned to it, or voice from the front, one report is enough): searches there like calling. Unknown (stopped while roaming, then silence): looks around once, listening hear_listen_s per view; a report during a view → turns there, listens, drives there. Silence all round → search ends (sad). Lockout call_repeat_s driving in pet with the room map (search, calling, back to start) the planner gives the path (like home); the Bahnprüfung still brakes. Calling goal: if the room map shows a wall within 1 m ahead and more room behind, he searches behind (front and back sound the same); the goal ends before the wall. No path, or a detour over 1.5× the straight line → the other direction call without usable direction, room map with confirmed pose (call_openings 4, 2026-11-22) calls from another room arrive at ~0° whatever his heading (reverb, mics 4 mm apart). Instead of driving straight: next opening of the room map (border to unknown, frontier.next_goal in the planner thread, visited ones excluded, none with a path shorter than call_min_m 0.3 m; if he had turned toward the sound, openings off that direction cost call_dir_s_per_deg 0.1 s/° extra, 2026-11-22) → drive there with the path follower of home (tight spots, push, replanning; gives up only after two replans while stuck, time from the path length) → look around and listen (hear_listen_s standing per view, levels) → a person found there: drives to her like "come here" (no second call needed) → call_louder_db (3 dB) louder than so far = louder, either way on to the next opening; after call_openings openings or none left he stays and listens. Sound is not used while driving. Unit tests only search over, nobody found (seek_home, off since 2026-11-22; for a vanished person only with lost_home) drives back to the map start only with a start image (2026-11-22; the start is set on every stand-up and set-down, see mapping). The drive is home's (planner, pre-point, straight final run, measurement against the start image, pose correction). Without anchor or confirmed pose he stays where he is suddenly loud (hear_startle_db = 20 dB) after hear_quiet_s (8 s) of silence, nobody in view surprised, squeak, ducks 0.6 s, turns fast (turn_w). No retreat, no faint dozing, two reports in a row wakes: surprised, horch, detector back to active_hz lying after a faint air is not clear while someone speaks (last report < clear_s): eyes stay shut, no stand-up lying (set down from outside), two reports doubt, horch (direction is useless lying down) talking back: person in view (or just found by listening) speaks ≥ talk_min_events (2) reports, then pauses talk_pause_s (1.6 s) sound brabbeln, head tilt; at most every talk_repeat_s (7 s); with parrot_p (0.5) a learned voice sample instead, ≥ parrot_repeat_s (30 s) apart (audio.md) a voice sample gets confirmed (same phrase twice within 1 min while a person is in view, balancing or lying) or a confirmed one is recognized parrots it after parrot_delay_s (0.2 s), budgie-filtered, every time

Pi cost: a few comparisons per control step; the sound direction itself as in audio.md.

docs.title: Patches
docs.text: Patch Change 0001 memory bugs in proc handlers fixed; settings/motion_timeout_ms (kernel watchdog, default 0 = off) 0002 synchronous reads (completion instead of msleep(200)); IMU thread → imu, imu_log, serial_stats; UART raw mode in rc.local 0003 settings/force_yaw (pulsed heading hold): removed 2026-11-17, was never tested on the Rider. xgonav writes force_yaw = 0 only if an old driver still has the entry 0004 roll = roll angle in degrees (reg 0x36); old function (roll balance, 0x61) → roll_balance later wheel encoders (combined register 0x0d) → wheels, wheels_log; raw_reg diagnostics; calibration sends bytes 0/1 (was ASCII, inverted); pitch_calibration stream IMU/wheel stream of firmware patch 0014 (2026-11-08): settings/imu_stream_hz, frames type 0x14 → imu_log/wheels_log with the firmware's sample time; polling only as fallback 2026-11-17 read paths for firmware without firmware patch 0001 removed (IMU modes 0/1/2, wheel register 0x0c, settings/wheel_hz); yaw from the stream; force_yaw removed; dead code removed (xgo-lcd.c, xgo-lcd.h). Not installed on the Rider

docs.title: IMU / wheel read path (auto-detected at load)
docs.text:
Path Register Content Firmware Stream type 0x14 (see below) roll, pitch, yaw + wheel ticks with the firmware's sample time R-1.1.6 + firmware patch 0014 Polling (only without stream) 0x0d roll, pitch, yaw (float) + left/right ticks (int32) + t_ms (uint32), 24 B, at imu_hz R-1.1.6 + firmware patch 0001
  • Detection of 0x0d at load compares against fresh single-register reads (roll/pitch within 2°, yaw within 10°).
  • Firmware without 0x0d: IMU and wheels only via the stream, warning in the kernel log. The older read paths (single registers 0x62–0x64, 12-byte block from 0x62, 0x65, wheels via 0x0c) were removed 2026-11-17.
  • serial_stats: imu_block = 3 (0x0d can be polled) or 0; wheels = wheel ticks available (0x0d or stream seen).
  • Timestamp: CLOCK_MONOTONIC, end of reply minus transfer time ((n + 8) × 10 bits at 115200). Firmware 0014: a 0x0d reply comes from a snapshot renewed every 10 ms, so the value can be up to 10 ms older than this.

docs.title: IMU/wheel stream (firmware patch 0014)
docs.text: Item Value Enable settings/imu_stream_hz > 0: the IMU thread writes register 0x11 = rate every second (firmware stops after 5 s without a byte from the Pi and after an ESP restart); 0 writes 0 once Frame 55 00 22 14 11 + 26 B + checksum 00 AA: seq u16, t_us u32 (micros() right after the IMU read), roll/pitch/yaw float, ticks wheel 11/21 s32 (little endian) Rates firmware: 0..250 Hz, divider of its IMU read (~333 Hz on the RiderPi), intervals at 100 Hz 9–12 ms Time offset = receive time − 34 B transfer (2.95 ms) − t_us; minimum taken immediately when lower, window minimum every ~2 s (follows ESP clock drift); t_us unwrapped (71 min overflow), ESP restart resets the offset Logs each frame → one imu_log and one wheels_log sample (fw_ms = t_us / 1000) Polling skipped while the stream is active: last frame younger than max(200 ms, 2.5 send intervals) (fixed 200 ms until 2026-11-17); otherwise 0x0d (firmware without stream, stream lost). Emulator, --wheels --combo --stream=5, 20 s: 11 polled samples between 100 stream frames (start-up before the first frame only), 17–18 before Heading /proc/XGORider/yaw is set from every frame (whole degrees, truncated like register 0x68, only while balancing); register 0x68 is polled only without stream (saves ~5 requests/s) Stats serial_stats: stream, stream_gaps (seq gaps = frames dropped by the firmware), stream_hz, stream_active, stream_offset_us Userspace xgonav [imu] stream_hz writes the setting at start; imu_log format unchanged

docs.title: /proc/XGORider
docs.text: File Mode Format / range Register speed_x w u8 0..255, 128 = stop; arms motion watchdog 0x30 speed_z w u8 0..255, 128 = stop; arms watchdog 0x32 height rw u8 0..255 (web UI min 43); read: last written value, empty until first write; not reset when the firmware stands up at 128 0x35 roll rw int −20..20 °, mapped linearly to 0..255; read: last written value, empty until first write 0x36 roll_balance w 0/1 0x61 action w u8; R-1.1.6+patch: 1..6 actions, 237 restart the ESP32 (firmware patch 0018, refused while balancing), 253 stand up from lying, 254 disarm/emergency stop, 255 arm, 0 = no action 0x3e leds/0..leds/3 w #RRGGBB 0x69..0x6c battery r % 0x01 state r firmware state: 1 = balancing, 254 = lying (set down by action 254, LEDs orange), 0 = fallen (tilt, LEDs red), 253 = ready (disarmed, starts when upright), 250 = low battery, 251 = actuator fault, 252 = other fault; names in robot.FW_ZUSTAND yaw r integer degrees, only updated while balancing; from the stream, without stream from register 0x68 every sleep_ms_on_loop buttons r bit mask, 1 = pressed: A = 1 (GPIO 17), B = 2 (22), C = 4 (23), D = 8 (24); polled every sleep_ms_on_loop. A+B together = orderly_poweroff (driver). C+D held 3 s = Wi-Fi setup (wifi-setup.md) imu r seq t_ns roll pitch yaw (millidegrees), newest sample imu_log r last 128 samples, oldest first wheels r seq t_ns ticks_left ticks_right fw_ms (fw_ms only with 0x0d) wheels_log r last 64 samples serial_stats r frames bad timeouts unsolicited imu_seq imu_hz imu_block wheels wheel_seq stream stream_gaps stream_hz stream_active stream_offset_us tunnel_rx tunnel_drop tunnel_tx pi_ip (one per line) raw_reg rw, root write "0x0b 16" (addr, len), read "0x0b 16: 00 11 .."; read-only diagnostics any ble rw, root BLE tunnel of firmware patch 0025 (ble.md). Blocking read (or poll) = one record: byte 0 kind (0 data, 1 BLE connected, 2 disconnected) + ≤ 23 bytes, buffer ≥ 24 bytes; returns 0 when the module unloads. Write = bytes to the BLE client, sent in 23-byte chunks every 4 ms. Reader: xgo-ble 0x17, frames type 0x15

docs.text: File Default Range / effect motion_timeout_ms 0 (off) 0..60000; no speed_x/speed_z write for this long → stop imu_hz 50 0..200, 0 = off; polling rate of 0x0d, used only without stream imu_stream_hz 0 0..250; > 0 = firmware stream (0014), polling only as fallback led_brightness −1 (never written) 0..255: global LED multiplier n/256 of firmware patch 0016 (reg 0x12; firmware default 32, former fixed value 64). Older firmware ignores it ip_dev wlan0 network interface (name ≤ 8 characters) whose first IPv4 the driver reports to the ESP32 for BLE (firmware patch 0025, reg 0x18): on change and every 3 s from the main loop; 0.0.0.0 without address. docs.title: UART raw mode (required)
docs.text:
deploy/rc.local: 

stty -F /dev/ttyAMA0 115200 cs8 -cstopb -parenb -brkint -imaxbel -opost -onlcr -isig -icanon -iexten \
  -echo -echoe -echok -echoctl -echoke -ixon -ixoff -icrnl -inlcr -igncr -istrip min 0 time 1

docs.title: ESP32 protocol assumptions
docs.text:
• Replies carry the requested address.
  • Writes are not acknowledged.
  • Internal update rate of firmware attitude values unknown.
  • serial_stats counts timeouts and unsolicited frames.

driver-test/run.sh kernel_module [seconds=6] [imu_hz=50] [--wheels --combo] [--stream[=HZ] | --stream-off] [--tunnel] [--faults]
--tunnel (firmware 0025): the emulator sends data through the BLE tunnel (frames type 0x15), the harness echoes it via register 0x17; checked complete and in order next to polling and stream (2026-11-20 with --stream --faults: 892 bytes in 45 records, none dropped). docs.title: FloorNet
docs.text: Self-trained network for the floor boundary, one row per image column. Status: the only floor boundary; decides alone on the RiderPi since 2026-11-10 and drives with it. Without the network (file or C++ core missing, self-test or runtime failure) the Rider is blind and does not drive by itself (docs/configuration.md).

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
Item Value Input 640×480 BGR, rows 137–478, 2:1 average → 320×171 Structure 3×3 stem, 6 depthwise-separable blocks, rows collapsed, column head (1×1, 1×3, 1×1) Output 80 columns (8 px each), 64 row bins each over rows 215–480 (up to p11h: 205–480): 1.4 px at the top, about 9 px at the bottom; best bin refined with a parabola Bin range per net row_top in the run's netz.json (missing = 205, runs up to p11h); every .bin carries its own bin centres, so the Rider decodes old and new nets correctly When only while balancing; lying or set down there is no boundary and the net is not run. Pitch in training: train.py --nick_korr 5 removes the measured pitch (up to 5°) per frame, --nick_zufall 5 adds random ±5°, --roll 3 random ±3° roll about the image centre; image and label move together (geom_shift, test test_geom_shift_bild_und_label_passen) Size 30 k parameters, 17.8 MMACs (f2_s in bench_kern.cpp) Time, untrained, CM4 next to YOLO at 12 Hz 13.6 ms mean, 17.3 ms p95; YOLO 119 → 136 ms Inference C++ with NEON (xgonav/native/floornet.cpp, floornet_kern.h), float32, no framework, self-test at load

Field of view: tools/floornet/sichtfeld.py writes two RGBA masks (640×480) to lay over any undistorted input image; --bild a.jpg --out b.png makes a preview, --meta <run>/meta.jsonl (or --nick/--roll in degrees) first rotates the frame to pitch 0 and roll 0 (homography about the image centre), so the drawn horizon meets the real one. Regenerate after changing net.py or the camera geometry.

Pitch sign: pitch_dev 0 means IMU pitch = pitch_ref_deg (−5.0°); there the camera looks tilt_deg (5.18°) up, so the horizon lies 28 rows below the centre. Only the sum matters: at IMU pitch 0 the camera is level (0.18°). While driving pitch_dev is typically −2 to −4°, so the horizon sits at rows ~245–256 in raw frames.

Mask Shows img/floornet_maske.png green: network input rows 137–478; red over it: output range rows 215–480 (nets from p11i; up to p11h 205), so the mixed colour is input and output, pure green is input only (context); output with 80 column lines and the 64 bin edges as a scale on the left; white dashed: the 5 freespace.sectors img/floornet_maske_entfernung.png nominal (pitch 0, cruise height, camera 121 mm): horizon (row 268) and floor distances 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 m (rows 346 / 306 / 294) img/floornet_beispiel1.png, img/floornet_beispiel2.png both masks over a kitchen (tiles, pitch −2.2°, roll −1.0°) and an office (carpet, pitch −3.2°, roll +2.0°) frame, each rotated to pitch 0 / roll 0 first; black border = outside the original frame

Constraints from the kernel: no ReLU and no bias after the depthwise convolution, residual before the ReLU of the 1×1 layer, 1×1 output channels divisible by 8. BatchNorm exists only in training; net.fold folds it into the weights.

docs.text: File Purpose tools/floornet/comfy_batch.py, comfy_prompt*.txt ComfyUI (Qwen-Image-Edit paints the floor green) over many frames, stage 1; see below tools/floornet/ids_fahrt.py frame list of raw recordings for comfy_batch.py --ids: every n-th frame, standing frames dropped tools/floornet/stage2.py, inseln.py green edits → masks (stage 1 → 2, floor_mask, --gruen for the green lead); count and show islands and holes in masks, changes nothing tools/floornet/stage3.py stage 2 → 3: per pixel column only what is unbroken from the bottom edge; no islands or holes remain tools/floornet/stage3_npz.py stage 3 → label files for train.py: one row per 8 px strip (majority), filters as comfy_npz.py; frames from --data/<run>, camera geometry (only for metres in evaluation and distance weights) from --config (Rider TOML), camera height from height_mm in meta.jsonl; --gesichtet keeps only frames the user has seen tools/floornet/comfy_npz.py label building shared with stage3_npz.py; drops frames lying down, tilting (> 10 % of columns above row 215, ROW_MIN = net.ROW_TOP), torn masks (> 6 jumps > 40 px), dark (mean grey < 12) sorting out (from stage 2 on) nothing is deleted. docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
On kimmy (~/floornet), after new runs went through ComfyUI and were looked at in the viewer:

cd tools/floornet
python stage2.py ~/floornet/stage1_p11 ~/floornet/stage2_p11 --gruen 30 --jobs 4
python stage3.py ~/floornet/stage2_p11 ~/floornet/stage3_p11
python stage3_npz.py ~/floornet/stage3_p11 --config rider.toml --out labels/ --jobs 8 \
    --gesichtet ~/floornet/stage1_p11/gesichtet.txt --fahrten <dated runs>
python train.py --labels labels/ --out run/ --train <runs> --val "" --dist 0.005 --yaw 0.5 --epochs 200 --lr 1.5e-3 \
    --far_w 2 --smooth_w 2 --seed 1 [--nick_korr 5 --nick_zufall 5 --roll 3]
python eval_labels.py run/ --labels ~/floornet/stage3_p11d_pruef --fahrten explore10,explore11,explore12
python export.py run/floornet.pt --out models/floornet_<name>.bin

Only runs the user has looked at go into training. Test runs are never trained: explore10–12 (final test), streife1 + unten*, explore2–9. Training (200 epochs, ~36 k frames) takes about 9 minutes on the GPU; one seed varies by about ±1–3 points under 1 m.

On the Rider models/floornet.bin is a symlink into models/floornet/ ([freespace] net_dir); copy further nets there as <name>.bin (.tmp + mv, never cp onto the symlink) and pick one in the web (Bodenmodell, idle/manual only, no restart; cost on the Pi: one load + self-test on demand, nothing per frame except an uncontended lock around the inference). deploy/install.sh copies new and changed files from models/floornet/.

Spike removal in the decoder ([freespace] net_outlier_px, default 25, 0 = off; net.decode(logits, outlier_px, outlier_ratio) in PyTorch, decode in native/floornet.cpp, both tested against each other): the raw output has 1–3 column wide jumps at vertical high-contrast edges, the output there is bimodal. A column further than net_outlier_px rows from the median of the 7 columns around it takes the best bin within ±2 bins of that median, if the probability mass there (5 bins) is at least net_outlier_ratio (0.3) of the mass at its own peak. Columns without a second peak keep their value (narrow obstacles). Cost on the Rider: a 7-value median per column, exp only in outlier columns.

explore10–12 (never trained), 4551 frames < 1 m falsely free / blocked frames with spike down / up plain decode 5.4 / 6.2 % 6.1 / 2.1 % spike removal 5.4 / 5.8 % 1.0 / 0.6 %

Spike = column more than 25 rows from the 7-column median; the count includes real narrow obstacles. Measured 2026-11-10 against stage 3 labels.

docs.title: Labels from ComfyUI
docs.text:
ComfyUI on kimmy (service comfyui, ~29 GB VRAM next to LM Studio) has only image generation and editing models, no segmentation or depth. Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 with the 4-step Lightning LoRA recolours the floor green; the green mask gives the boundary per column (lowest run of floor from the bottom, gaps up to 6 rows bridged). 3.6 s per frame, first load 2.5 min.

python comfy_batch.py --prompt prompt_standard.txt --ids ids.txt --edits <stage1> --out <stage1>

comfy_batch.py keeps every edit (<edits>/<run>/<frame>.png), so masks can be recomputed without the model. Seed fixed (SEED = 1); repaints in the viewer use a random seed.

Prompt Use T1 (comfy/prompte/t1.txt, prompt_standard.txt links to it) standard since 2026-11-20 (rug set) 11 (comfy_prompt11.txt) all runs up to lauf21 (run 20261120-115634): only the bare floor surface is recoloured, rugs and things on the floor stay unchanged 10 (comfy_prompt10.txt) before 2026-11-11; painted rugs and things lying on the floor green

Input and mask: --eingang g0h for dark frames (green channel 0, larger of R and B set to the grey value; colour kept for rugs, dark green-tinted frames not black), mask with hue and saturation and green lead G − max(R, B) ≥ 30 (stage2.py --gruen 30), then stage3.py. The green channel alone (G > 0) fails: the image decoder leaves small green values on unpainted pixels. Low thresholds count the faint green shimmer the model adds to walls next to the floor (unten2/002400: walls up to 48, floor from 170). floor_mask requires V ≥ 30: below that the hue is noise, above it floor painted dark green in shadow counted as blocked.

Prompt rule Finding "recolour the floor, add nothing" reflections and lamp glare become floor naming rugs or "a small robot" the model paints them into the frame (robot in ~50 % of frames): never name what should not appear floor under furniture only where the gap is higher than 18 cm far fewer columns running under sofas, chair bases and low shelves baseboards and skirting tiles are wall tile skirting of the same material is no longer painted floor ends at the front edge of sofa / chair base no gain on 60 frames, worse on random ones: dropped

Known teacher errors: a tile-clad step riser seen from close by is painted as floor, as is floor visible under an overhanging sofa. These labels are no fall or step protection. The network is weakest directly in front of plain walls filling the frame (columns jump).

Brightening (2026-11-19, aufhellen.py): --aufhellen S runs Zero-DCE (DCE-Net from keras-io/low-light-image-enhancement, ported to torch, weights ~/floornet/comfy/zerodce.npz on kimmy, not in the repo) on dark frames (brightness < --hell_ab) before the chain; curve step scaled by S (1 = Keras example, which lifted mean grey ~63 → 188 and was judged too strong; 0.5 → ~128, 0.25 → ~94). --dunkel farbe|g0h picks the chain for dark frames. Not used: no frame better than without. Moss-Image-Edit instead of Qwen: no frame better than the Qwen green image (user, 40 probe frames).

docs.title: Labels from geometry (probe 2026-11-18)
docs.text:
Decision 2026-11-20: not adopted. Judged on the images, the stage 3 p11 labels (Qwen green image) are better than every geometry teacher (MoGe-2, all DA3 variants); training labels stay on the p11 pipeline.

tools/floornet/geo_label.py, model Ruicheng/moge-2-vitl-normal (MIT, 331 M parameters; pip install git+https://github.com/microsoft/MoGe.git).

Step Rule Points MoGe-2 with fov_x = hfov_deg, principal point at the image centre (matches CamGeometry) Plane RANSAC (256 planes from 3 points) on points below the IMU horizon + 15 rows; only planes within 8° of the IMU pitch and with distance 0.6–3.0 × cam_h in model units (MoGe puts the Rider camera 1.2–1.7× too high); refined 3× by smallest eigenvector of inliers (tolerance 10 % of cam_h) Scale everything scaled so the plane lies exactly cam_h below the camera; fewer than 2000 inliers → median scale of the run so far, IMU pitch (art ersatz), shown in the images only and dropped from the label file Pixel class floor h ≤ 2.5 cm, including everything below the plane (no drop class, user decision); obstacle 2.5 cm < h < 18 cm; above 18 cm ignored (table, high sofa) Row per strip free floor from the bottom (majority per 8 px strip, gaps ≤ 6 rows, same as mask_rows); if the 16th-nearest obstacle pixel of the strip is nearer, the row where the floor has that forward distance (foot point under a low sofa edge)

Per frame on kimmy: model 80 ms at batch 8 (9.9 GB VRAM), CPU 12 ms in threads (--jobs) next to the GPU; ~13 frames/s overall.

explore10–12 vs. stage 3 p11 (1384 frames, skala_hi 3.0, 2.4 % ersatz) median abs. diff geometry > 15 cm freer > 15 cm tighter 0–0.5 m 2 cm 7 % 9 % 0.5–1.0 m 6 cm 7 % 16 % 1.0–1.5 m 13 cm 12 % 32 % 1.5–2.5 m 31 cm 20 % 55 % 
python tools/floornet/geo_label.py fahrten --runs explore10,explore11,explore12 --jedes 2 --config rider.toml --out geo_lab
Known gap Effect Rugs geometrically floor, for the Rider an obstacle: false free on rugs Step down counted as floor (no drop class): geometry labels never block a downward step Scale camera height 121–150 mm is unusual for MoGe; only the plane fit sets the scale

Tests: tests/test_floornet_geo.py (rendered point maps: wall, box, low sofa edge, table, step down, pitch error, scale error, holes; with a fake model; depth maps via --tiefe).

docs.text:
tools/floornet/da3_tiefe.py (own venv ~/floornet/da3/.venv on kimmy, DA3 needs numpy < 2) writes depth + conf per frame; geo_label.py --tiefe DIR builds the point map from it with the Rider f and image centre. DA3 depth is relative, so --skala_lo 0.2 --skala_hi 5. Comparison page: tools/floornet/da3_seite.py → ~/floornet/da3/index.html (port 8765, /da3/).

Variant Licence GPU per frame Own plane (of 1384) MoGe-2 (for reference) MIT 80 ms 1351 DA3METRIC-LARGE, single Apache 2.0 50 ms 1165 DA3-LARGE-1.1, single CC BY-NC 4.0 58 ms 1322 DA3-LARGE-1.1, windows of 8 consecutive frames CC BY-NC 4.0 37 ms 1098

vs. stage 3 p11 on the 940 frames where all have an own plane (> 15 cm freer / tighter than p11), all with --entzerrt 1:

Band MoGe-2 metric L-1.1 single L-1.1 window 8 0–0.5 m 3.3 / 4.7 % 2.4 / 2.5 % 3.3 / 0.6 % 2.5 / 0.0 % 0.5–1.0 m 6.7 / 11.3 % 8.9 / 9.9 % 5.0 / 6.4 % 8.3 / 7.6 % 1.0–1.5 m 12.0 / 27.9 % 31.0 / 17.5 % 5.6 / 28.8 % 12.4 / 27.4 % 1.5–2.5 m 19.9 / 52.1 % 47.9 / 33.1 % 9.1 / 57.7 % 17.1 / 55.8 %

Filled border of the lens table (--entzerrt, default 1): pixels whose source lies outside the camera image (camera.lens_source; right edge 24–26 px at floor-line height, 13 px at the bottom, plus the bottom ~10 rows of the right half) are left out of the plane fit; strips whose centre below the horizon is mostly filled take the row of the nearest real strip (line continues flat), widened by one strip inwards (MoGe kinks ~8 px before the filled border, explore10/008606). MoGe tighter than p11: 0–0.5 m 10.3 → 4.7 → 0.8 %, 0.5–1.0 m 11.3 → 7.4 %; DA3 unchanged.

Bent-up near floor (rand_rampe, --rand, default 1): DA3 sometimes lifts the floor near the bottom edge (explore11/010011: h 0 → 9 cm over the bottom 100 rows), the band turns obstacle and the line drops to row 480. Per strip, an obstacle band touching the bottom counts as floor if at least min_px rows of floor follow directly above it and the band rises towards the bottom (bottom quarter > top quarter + 1 mm). A flat box top at the edge stays obstacle. 010011: row 480 → 303–324; totals unchanged (DA3-L-1.1 below 1 m 5.0 % freer / 5.7 % tighter).

Windows of 8 do not make the line steadier from frame to frame (median change 4.6 vs. 5.0 cm single, p11 5.1 cm) and lose planes. explore10 stays ~29 % freer than p11 below 1 m for every geometry teacher (rugs).

docs.title: Hardware test status
docs.text: Item Status Driver patches 0001/0002, IMU ~49 Hz, kernel watchdog tested Wheel encoders (0x0d), odometry scale tested (tape measure, 215 cm) Wheel heading vs IMU 2026-11-05, 184 s / 15 m / 25 turns: slope 1.000, 3° apart at the end (track 0.090 m fits) Camera geometry, lens shading measured Manual driving (web UI) tested follow tested 2026-11-02 (runs 3–8, max_v 0.10–0.15); works, path check blocked in some runs. Search at the last known position (planner, look around, since 2026-11-22): simulator only (--scene zwei) explore frontier mapping, three recorded RiderPi runs 2026-11-06, see below. Map not yet usable: ends too early home 2026-11-05, 3 tries: did not reach the start. Stop/turn/start cycles and changing plans (45 s without progress), then stuck 1.3 m before the start at a gap the path check considers too narrow; afterwards changed (path keeping, LocalMap obstacles in planning, curve driving), not retested approach not tested on the Rider. Sim (2026-11-13, standing chair, also --rider --dyn --wheels --kanten): stops ~0.55 m in front, 0 collisions. Ends when the distance estimate is ≤ approach_dist_m + dist_deadband and aligned for 1 s, or when safety/arc check hold it < 0.3 m beyond that for 3 s. Explores reactively until the target is seen; no fall protection (stairs) pet simulator and unit tests only, not run on the Rider. Approach thresholds not tuned on real footage; cats and dogs from 12.8 cm camera height untested. A person standing < 1.9 m has no head in the image, so "kneeling" is inferred from the box top. Reverse is blind. Auto stand-up relies on IMU, wheels, /proc/XGORider/state and an empty image; the lying camera view is limited, floor or steps in front are not checked. A direct echo 254 > action without POST /stop is not noticed. Search/roam (seek_m, roam_m) (RiderPi: no distance limit) drive via the planner with a room map, otherwise straight, and stop at obstacles; the last position comes from the noisy foot point (±0.3 m standing). Following a trusted person and the drive home with start image (2026-11-22): simulator only; call search via the openings of the map (2026-11-22): unit tests only; the start image measurement gave no correction in the simulator runs without --rider (pet and home: too few matches/depth) Fear of the dark (dunkel.py) simulator and unit tests only, not run on the Rider. Thresholds from raw-run brightness, not from a drive into darkness; turning in the dark relies on IMU/wheel heading, the floor model sees little there. docs.text:
• Web UI has no authentication.
  • Room map drifts (no markers).
  • Web attitude model: legs show the last written height/roll setpoints, not measured positions (firmware does not report them). State 254 (Absetzen) shows legs at the firmware minimum (45 mm extension) as an assumption.   • Body height and camera geometry: xgonav reads /proc/XGORider/height every 0.2 s and follows new writes, also from the web (before 2026-11-07 it ignored them: drive unten3 ran at camera height 151 mm while the geometry assumed 128 mm, distances ~18 % too far). While the Rider is down the firmware zeroes its height every tick and stands up at its centre 128 (≈ 90 mm); /proc still shows the old value, so xgonav assumes 90 mm after each stand-up until the next write (behaviors send their height again). It is the setpoint, not the leg position (legs need ~1 s). A web write of the same value as before the stand-up is not detected.
  • Body height limited to u8 205 (web UI, API, xgonav; provisional). The firmware drives only 55..200 (main.cpp, range seen in training), so 201..205 act as 200 (≈ 107 mm). Setpoint 235 on 2026-11-06: firmware stop, state 252 (not tilt, fall, low battery or servo loss; IMU, control gap > 30 ms or invalid control output; cause open, single event). 205 held ~2 s, 225 ~1 s. Firmware itself accepts 0..255; direct writes to /proc/XGORider/height are not limited.
  • Leg calibration buttons removed (saving with slack legs overwrote flash zero points, 2026-11-02).
  • Battery: driver powers off below 8 % (low_batt_level); full image processing draws more than the charging dock supplies.

Not driven on the Rider Cost 1 + clear_cost near obstacles + unknown_cost for unknown cells; line-of-sight shortcut only if not more expensive (maximum and sum) Thread PlannerWorker (cores = cpu.freespace_cpus); replan every replan_s 2 s and after 3 s without 5 cm progress Path keeping current path kept while free and ≤ keep_factor × new + 0.3 m; dropped after getting stuck Local obstacles confirmed LocalMap points within 1.5 m (what _arc_check brakes for) are blocked for planning (use_localmap) Following pure pursuit, lookahead 0.5 m, home.kp_turn 1.5/s; turn in place only above 75° error until below 25°, otherwise drive the curve at ≥ 30 % speed Tight spot occupied map cell within tight_m 0.21 m of the pose or of the path up to 0.45 m ahead (normal paths keep 0.23 m): lookahead 0.2 m, speed × 0.6, turn in place above 30° until below 10°, path check with map.radius_tight_m 0.08 m instead of 0.18 m, and aim at the middle between the nearest confirmed LocalMap points left and right ahead (the room map places a narrow gap centimetres off). Cost on the Pi: four 11 × 11 cell windows per control step while following a path Goal within arrive_m 0.15 m, then turn to start heading (align_heading), status „am Start angekommen“, stands Failure max_fail 3 consecutive plans without path → stop, „kein Weg zum Start“ Safety safety() and _arc_check() apply as in explore Requires freespace.enabled, grid.enabled, running pipeline Accuracy limited by map drift: arrives at the map start; real error = pose error. With [startbild] the pose is measured against the start image at the end (below)

docs.title: Start image check (xgonav/startbild.py, [startbild])
docs.text: Item Value Anchor grey image + SIFT features while the Rider stands at the start point (≤ 3 cm, ≤ 5°, not turning); once per start point, only after the roll calibration after stand-up (Robot.levelled); dropped when the start is set anew, on set-down/fall (may be carried) and when the pose becomes unknown (2026-11-22) Start point set on every stand-up (once standing still 1 s after the roll calibration) and set-down, in every mode, never on a mode change (App._start_tick, 2026-11-22); not with a locked map or unknown pose; "Start hier" in the web as before Ending of home path to a pre-point 0.40 m before the start → turn to start heading → straight onto the start (grey image every 4 cm) → stand 0.5 s → measure → if > 4 cm left: turn to the start, drive (once) → turn to the start heading within end_deg 2° (stop on overshoot or after 8 s) Measurement own thread on cpu.render_cpus: end image vs. images 0.1–0.3 m earlier, triangulated with the odometry of the straight run (mm-exact over decimetres); anchor matched to these 3D points; anchor pose solved for x, y, heading plus small pitch/roll residuals, camera height fixed (124 mm measured); cross-check free 6-DOF PnP Camera model undistorted image, f from hfov, principal point image centre, tilt + pitch_dev, IMU roll (without it the 3D points were rotated by the end roll, +2.3° in run 20261119-144940), lens cam_fwd ahead of the axle Gate ≥ min_inl 30 consistent matches, correction ≤ 0.5 m / 15°, pitch/roll residual ≤ 1°, 6-DOF within 5 cm; otherwise no correction, status says why Correction GridMap.shift_pose(k) with k ∘ measured anchor pose = anchor pose at the start; behaviour heading shifted by the same angle Web colour copy of the anchor frame (once per anchor), GET /startbild.jpg (JPEG once per anchor, on request), status startbild.bild = anchor number (0 = none); shown below the room map, hidden without anchor Offline tools/start_abgleich.py (same code on recordings). Run 20261119-144940 (37 m): end measured 8.0 cm forward / 10.2 cm left / −4.8°, user with folding rule 5 / 11 cm, odometry −3 / +2 cm. Short pairs of the same run (odometry nearly exact): accepted ones within 1.8 cm Simulator tests/sim_run.py home 120 --wheels --rider --yaw-scale 1.01 --set startbild.enabled=True: true distance to the start at the end 6.5 cm (without: 22 cm), map heading error 0.9° (3.5°) Rider run 2026-11-19 161006: measured 19 cm / −5.1°, 131 matches, 11.4 s on the CM4; end ~1 cm ahead of the start (user), but turned −9.5° (old 10° tolerance) → end_deg Cost on the Pi nothing while driving; ~1 ms grey image for the anchor and every 4 cm of the straight run; measurement SIFT on 1 + 5 images while standing (0.25 s on the PC, CM4 not measured)

docs.title: Route and patrol (xgonav/route.py, mode patrol)
docs.text: Item Value Map lock set when explore ends or patrol starts, POST /map/lock; locked: observations and the driven path do not change the map, the pose still moves. explore refuses a locked map Map id map_id in the npz; a route file with another id is ignored Route file <grid.file>.route.json: points, loop, zones, written atomically together with the map Point check on known floor, outside inflate_m, reachable from the start, outside zones; otherwise the route is rejected with a message No-go zones polygons in map coordinates. Planner and frontier never enter them plus inflate_m, _arc_check stops an arc that would come within map.radius_m 0.18 m (moving away stays allowed). All modes except manual. They drift with the pose: no replacement for a physical barrier Dark zones GridMap.dark_zones: rectangles set by fear of the dark during explore (docs/display-emotions.md), same effect as no-go zones via GridMap.all_zones(), expire after [dunkel] zone_s, never saved, not editable; violet in the map image, dunkelzonen in the map stats Patrol points in order, pause_s 1.5 s each; stuck: replan, then back up and skip the point; contact, max_fail plans without a way or point_timeout_s 90 s: skip. No point reached in a lap, or end of a non-loop route: to the start Near enough stuck within home.near_m 0.5 m of a target counts as arrived: the path check clearance can make a free target unreachable Start only standing and with user confirmation that the Rider is at the start point: the pose jumps to the start, which removes drift. Battery ≥ 40 %. Back at 30 %, set down at 15 % (action 254) Status JSON patrol: zustand, punkt, von, runde, erreicht, ausgelassen, ende; grid: gesperrt, map_id, route, zonen

docs.title: Mapping a room (--mode explore, xgonav/frontier.py)
docs.text:
Item Value Start one full turn at explore.scan_w Speed explore.v 0.20 (≈ 36 cm/s at vx_limit 1.8) to goals and back to the start (home.v 0.15); exceeds robot.max_v in mode explore only. Tight spots × home.tight_v, wander at behavior.cruise_v. Slows down towards the path end unless the next goal is already planned. RiderPi 2026-11-11: two runs at 0.30, no contact Frontier reachable free cell next to unknown; groups ≥ min_cluster_m 0.4 m. Only when none of those is left: groups close to obstacles (within home.inflate_m, e.g. the mouth of a 25 cm gap, 3–5 cells) ≥ squeeze_cluster_m 0.15 m with ≥ min_unknown_m2 0.05 m² of connected unknown behind. Reachability from the room map only, the local map only shapes the path Choice nearest first: smallest drive time + turn time (bearing to the spot / turn_dps; 15 since 2026-11-14 so that straight ahead wins: 90° weigh like 2.1 m of driving, 40 before and in the simulator); unknown area within gain_radius_m counts as at most gain_bonus_s 3 s less (full from gain_ref_m2 2 m²). The goal stays until reached or gone and moves with its group, no switching by score. Until 2026-11-11 area / time: on the RiderPi four trips of 3.5–9.6 m across known floor Near the goal within roll_m 1.0 m: replan every roll_every_s 0.4 s, alternating between following the receding frontier and planning the goal after this one (from the goal, without its frontier). On arrival with the frontier in view (± pass_view_deg 40°) and that plan ≤ pass_age_s 3 s old: drives on without stopping. Every goal change is logged (Erkunden: ...) Tight-only goals compete with the others at tight_penalty_s 3 s extra (since 2026-11-15; before and in the simulator, -1: only when no goal with clearance is left, which made him turn around for a goal behind him while a tight spot lay straight ahead); at most tight_max 10 per run (3 until 2026-11-15 and in the simulator: holes in drawn walls look like gaps; RiderPi 2026-11-15 left 10 spots behind tight places with 3) Arrival stops standoff_m before the frontier, turns towards it, settle_s; no new goal within avoid_r_m 0.3 m of the spot Driven ground cells within driven_free_r_m of the driven path stay passable for the planner despite occupied specks and inflate_m; obstacles the local map sees now still block Contact command > 0.08 but < 2 cm movement in 2.5 s (normal start-up takes up to 1.8 s): treated as contact, back up and block the goal at once. Wheel slip hides it Stuck no 5 cm progress or 10° turn in 3 s: replan without the old path; again, or goal_timeout_s: back up 0.8 s, block the goal. No goal left: wander_s reactive driving, at most max_wander times, then stop End nothing reachable, < min_growth_m2 new floor in no_growth_s, max_s, or min_battery. Then save and drive to the start (return_home). Arrived there after a way home of at least recheck_min_m 1 m, it searches once more (new floor was seen on the way; at most recheck_max 3 times per run, 0 = off) and only then reports the map as done Status JSON explore: zustand, stellen, gesperrt, befreit, ziel, ende Without room map explore drives reactively (Explore), as approach does while searching

Measuring: tools/map_eval.py record stores simulator observations, eval replays them through GridMap in seconds, with --set grid.x=a,b sweeps and --rays (boundary error per distance).

Built 2026-11-11, simulator and unit tests only; not installed on the Rider.

docs.title: Map matching (xgonav/reloc.py)
docs.text:
Running matching is wired into the app with [reloc] track = true (default on since 2026-11-12; RiderPi: off since 2026-11-14): reloc.Nachfuehrung runs in the GridWorker thread for every observation entered into the room map, never in the image loop. A correction shifts the map pose rigidly (GridMap.shift_pose, at most max_step_m 0.08 m / max_step_deg 3° per match) and the poses of queued observations. Locked map: the map itself is the reference; while mapping: a map state ≥ ref_age_s old. Status: grid.abgleich (abgleiche, angenommen, korrektur_m, korrektur_deg, haelt, zuletzt, unsicher, ms_max). The global search (start pose) is still offline only. Not driven. Tools (same class): tools/map_replay.py (variant abgleich=1), tools/reloc_eval.py, tools/map_eval.py reloc (docs/testing.md).

Part What Scan floor boundary points of the last seconds in the robot frame (ScanPuffer), same rays as GridMap.add_freespace; hits weighted 1 / (1 + (d / 0.8 m)²), samples on the free rays Field from a map state: closeness to the nearest wall (sigma 0.10 m); hits on known free floor and free samples through walls cost abgleich_lokal window ±0.30 m, ±8° around the odometry pose, one cv2.matchTemplate per heading. Corridor (pose slides along one direction): corrects across and heading only suche_global whole map, 3° / 0.10 m, best 8 refined; accepted only if unique "unsure" too little wall, too little known area, does not fit, slides, ambiguous, peak at the window border While mapping reference = map state at least 12 s old; nothing is entered while the remaining correction exceeds 0.10 m / 3°

Measured 2026-11-11 (PC; boundary from FloorNet floornet_s3.bin, 8 raw recordings, simulator with drift 3 % distance, 2 % turn, 0.1 °/s):

Case Result Simulator, second drive against the finished map of the first mean pose error 0.56 -> 0.25 m (raum), 0.78 -> 0.13 m (zwei) Simulator, global search, 15 s pieces of the second drive 4 right, 0 wrong, 18 unsure of 22 (square rooms: corners look alike); 30 s pieces in raum: 7 right, 0 wrong, 5 unsure Real recordings, matching while mapping cells between double walls 1949 -> 1532 over 8 drives (explore6: 472 -> 286, end pose moved 0.76 m; measured drift of that drive 0.75 m); part of the drop is observations not entered Real recordings, global search, piece cut out 5 right, 9 wrong, 98 unsure of 112: explore sees most places once, the rest of the map does not know the piece Real recordings, global search, piece kept in the map (upper bound) 32 right, 4 wrong (all explore6, wheel heading), 76 unsure Time on the PC field 2 ms, local match 3 ms, global search 42-75 ms; not measured on the Pi

Known weakness: in front of a single wall the position along the wall is not observable; in a synthetic test the match was accepted there (not flagged as sliding) and pulled the pose up to 0.18 m along the wall until a corner came into view.

Open: two drives through the same room in one map frame (real test of the global search), timing on the Pi, a RiderPi drive with track.
